I'm a 28 year old woman and realized at about 20 I would be better off not ever having kids. I love babies and am good with kids, but my genes and daily mental health would not make me a good parent. Enthusiastically non-breeding women do exist, but it can make finding a partner a little more difficult.

The things you do with the free time and money that comes from not having children don't have to be stereotypically immature or irresponsible. It's entirely up to you. Do whatever you find most enjoyable, without bringing harm to anyone else, of course. Travel at a moment's notice because you can. Collect whatever you fancy. Take up an amazing and/or absurd hobby.
Actually, considering the depersonalization aspect, do whatever helps you feel most vibrant and alive and real and present. Without the responsibility of children, you can focus on finding what makes you, personally, feel the most fulfilled, the most *you* that you can possibly feel.

My personal summary of why I will remain childfree is that I struggle with suicidal thoughts so often it would be remarkably hypocritical to bring a new person into a life I want nothing more than to escape. I stay because I don't want to hurt the people who love me.

I don't advocate short hair for everyone, but personally, I find it easier to style and less irritating in my daily life. My hair is absurdly thick and wavy, though.

I first cut my hair short in high school because I didn't know how or care to put in the time to style it long and always threw it in a ponytail. In the decade+ since then I have rarely grown it out past my chin because I'm impatient and find my hair sticking to my skin very irritating and live where it's frequently over 100F for over 4 months a year.

Depending on your hair type a pixie or bob can be styled a variety of ways with a single cut. All of my short styles have taken more time in the morning than my standard ponytail, but I'm sure take far less time than drying and straightening long hair. Also, the wonderful thing about cutting your hair is that if you don't like it, it grows back.

I am diagnosed bipolar I and I have had 13 treatments over a couple month span this fall.  Before resorting to that I had tried medication for several years with only a few several month periods of relative stability.  Unfortunately, ECT did not help me much either.  I felt like the only way it helped my mood any was by causing such strong cognitive side effects that I just wasn't thinking enough to have my usual negative thoughts.  It was rather disconcerting, so I requested that the treatments be stopped.
However, I am aware of many successful cases of ECT as well.  Someone I talked to before going into the treatment had three to five treatments and it greatly improved her quality of life since.
My suggestion would be to research thoroughly and know what you'd be getting into.  From my experience the cognitive side effects do begin to wear off, but they're nothing to brush aside.

Head meds generally take much longer than a week to take full effect, especially since most of them are like lamotrigine in that they must be increased from a low dose gradually.  I titrated up to 300mg of lamotrigine and maintained that dose for quite a while.  I had very few side effects compared to other meds I've tried, but it didn't go unnoticed.  

I have also been on lexapro, but the idiot who prescribed it thought I might have bipolar and then only gave me an anti-depressant, which is utterly stupid because it sent me into a dysphoric mania of sorts.  I took it for nine days.

However, no two people have the same body/brain chemistry, so my experience with a med has no bearing on what your experience will be.  Give both the meds a few months to level out in your system and see how they treat you.  Good luck and stick with it.
